<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/schema.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS), daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx`  _(via daysAgo (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via daysFromNow (literal, a string literal in CLOCK_FUNCTIONS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `current_user (literal, 44 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2c91ddd4335df2302bc64c1a03734eaece230d96` — the merge of head `5c58f75597e383a6e862864e7e0b1dfd81d28d64` into base `bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2c91ddd4335df2302bc64c1a03734eaece230d96 && git checkout 2c91ddd4335df2302bc64c1a03734eaece230d96
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133 5c58f75597e383a6e862864e7e0b1dfd81d28d64 && git checkout -B drift-repro bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133 && git merge --no-ff 5c58f75597e383a6e862864e7e0b1dfd81d28d64

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `89bb05733305e1dbb811edf9d331ddb4bcd6b6d8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/stored-expression-inputs.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, .changeset/32529-stored-expression-inputs.md (declaration lines and level only)

Delta round on record 6836331831 (PR #32701 at head `1215cab9`, PASS with should-fix 1 to 4 and nits 1 and 2), plus a full read of what the round changed. PR #32858 resumes from `1215cab9` with `origin/main` merged once (`a61f761f`); judged on the net diff against the merge-base `f770d664` (15 files, +655 −9). The round's own delta is seven files: the changeset, `rule-explanations.ts` (the two new entries only; the `field-no-consumers` hunk in a `1215cab9..89bb0573` diff is `main`'s), `stored-expression-inputs.ts` (one docblock line and the finding's last sentence), `validate-expressions.ts` (the served-body lookup and a docblock move), `validate-expressions.test.ts`, and the two blueprint comments. `authoring-rules.ts` and `index.ts` are unchanged since `1215cab9`.

Read, not reviewed (on `main` unless said): `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-expressions.ts` (the flags and the dry-run default), `packages/objectql/src/stored-expression-backfill.ts` (what `--changed` rewrites, and under which context), `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` and `lint.ts` (the `--strict` verdicts), `packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts` at this head (`objectsAsServed`, `objectsWithoutTiedFields`), `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (the key line and the arm reader), and HotCRM `src/sales/objects/forecast.object.ts`, `package.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `code-quality.yml` at HotCRM `8277e61`. Tests and the `.mdx` and changeset prose are the seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

Each item of 6836331831:

- **should-fix 1 (the `--strict` consequence): the text is discharged; the HotCRM carrier is still owed.** The PR body's risk line now says a `--strict` run fails on the two warnings, that the CLI has no per-rule switch, and that HotCRM `src/sales/objects/forecast.object.ts:152` `display_title` turns HotCRM's `objectstack lint --strict` step red at its next platform bump. Re-read at HotCRM `8277e61`: line 152 is the `record.?owner_id.?name` expression, `package.json:19` is `"lint": "objectstack lint --strict"`, and both workflows run it. The changeset replaces "print them and pass. Nothing that was accepted is refused." with "no build and no save that passed before is refused" and a sentence saying a `--strict` run fails on every warning, these two included, until the field changes or the step drops `--strict`. Both `os explain` entries say the same. `os validate --strict` is named beside `os lint --strict`, and it is true: `validate.ts` counts every registry finding that is not `info` in `strictFailing`. The changeset does not name HotCRM; it need not, the PR body and Acceptance notes do. What is not in my inputs is the carrier in HotCRM itself: the dev report lists it as "to be filed by the seat". See ③.
- **should-fix 2 (`--apply`): discharged as asked.** `--apply` and `--changed` are the command's real flags on `main` (`apply: Flags.boolean(... default is a read-only dry run)`, and its own example is `os migrate stored-expressions --changed --apply --yes --json`). The finding message, the cross-record `os explain` entry, the member's docblock and the changeset spell `os migrate stored-expressions --changed --apply` and say that without `--apply` the command is a dry run that writes nothing. No bare `--changed` spelling of this repair is left under `packages/lint`, `content` or this changeset. `os explain` now says the command "recomputes and writes" under `--apply` and "counts those rows and writes nothing" without it; both match the command's header. One new consequence of the corrected spelling is should-fix A in ④.
- **should-fix 3 (`Clause-②`): discharged.** The changeset line 7 and the PR body both carry, line-leading, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` followed by a dash and the three names: `STORED_EXPRESSION_CROSS_RECORD_INPUT`, `STORED_EXPRESSION_VOLATILE_INPUT`, and `ExprIssue.rule`. The spelling is one `clause2-line.mjs` reads: the key line matches at the line start, the value token is `yes`, and the arm reader takes `(widening)` as the first thing after it; `yes (widening)` is a listed spelling. The names are the diff's: `index.ts` exports the two constants, and the exported `ExprIssue` gains `rule?: string`. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.
- **should-fix 4 (an expression-bearing field an extension adds): discharged by stating the extent.** Acceptance notes carry an "Extent" paragraph (the walk covers `fieldList`, no pass reads `objectExtensions[].fields`, a hop THROUGH an extension's reference is counted, the gap is inherited from the whole field-formula pass), and the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet says "Not yet judged". The walk is not widened, as declared. The dev report (6837156594) measures it: the same `hours` field gives 1 `stored-expression-cross-record-input` when declared on the object and 0 when an `objectExtensions` entry adds it. The card for widening the walk is "to be filed by the seat"; see ③.
- **nit 1 (placement and the per-object `find`): discharged.** `judgeFieldFormula`'s docblock sits on the function again. The served body is `typedObjects[objectPosition]`, a counter incremented as the first statement of the object loop, so no `continue` can skip it. The position is sound: `objects` is `recordsOf(stack.objects)`, `objectsAsServed` states and keeps a one-to-one, in-order contract with that list on both its early return and its fold, `objectsWithoutTiedFields` maps without dropping, and nothing between the two declarations and the loop reassigns or mutates either array. Positional is also the stricter reading of two objects that share a name or have none; the `find` took the first match. The existing `objectIndex` cannot serve here (it is −1 for a map-form `objects`), so the counter is not a duplicate.
- **nit 2 (the blueprint comments): discharged.** The jsdoc over `FORMULA_STORAGE_RULE` and the test comment name both rule ids. The net diff of `solution-blueprint.zod.ts` is five added and three removed lines, all inside that jsdoc; no describe string and no export moves.

Unchanged since the prior record and re-read on the net diff: both findings are `severity: 'warning'`, `authoring-rules.ts` maps `i.rule ?? EXPRESSION_INVALID`, the stored-field test is the engine's (`type !== 'formula'` and an `expression`), and the hop index order is served body, declared fields, injected columns.

### ② Semver level

- **Level and kind agree.** `@objectstack/lint: patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` adds no narrowing arm, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed and none is present. PR body and changeset carry the same two declaration lines. This is the pairing of the precedent the PR cites (`.changeset/30633-flow-input-declaration-lint.md`).
- **Check-runs on this head: all 72 completed (59 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 1 `failure`); no other red.** The one is `PR-body guards` run 131523202422, and its only failure-level annotation is the duplicate-fix leg: "#32529, #32554 is already claimed by #32701", read while #32701 was still open. A second `PR-body guards` run on this head (131526545622, started after) is `success`. Both `Check Changeset` runs are `success`. Every other run is `success` or `skipped`, including `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8, `Test UI` 1/16 to 16/16, the type checks, the lint gates, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: empty.
- **Owed by the seat before landing, not in this diff: the HotCRM carrier.** The PR says the `display_title` disposition "is HotCRM's own card, reported to the seat". Nothing in my inputs shows that card exists. Without it HotCRM's lint step goes red at its next bump with no one holding the decision (relax the strict gate, or move the title to a snapshot written by a flow).
- **Owed by the seat, not in this diff: the card for widening the field walk to extension-added expression fields** (should-fix 4's other half; the dev report names it with the 1 against 0 measurement).
- Carried from the prior record, still for the seat: #32703's title says a cross-record input "is refused"; the published `STORED_EXPRESSION_RULE` describe on `main` names a `summary` as a route for a related record's value, which this PR's finding deliberately does not.
- `PR-body guards` carries two warnings beside its red leg: the claim leg is UNDETERMINED on #32529 and #32554 ("newest `Claim:` comment carries no parseable `Branch:` line"), and the branch `claude/project-thread-t5l85q` names no declared issue. Neither fails the check; both are the seat's to read.
- Dev deviation: the round is on a thread branch with a replacement PR, and the claims were re-posted to name it. The seat's to accept; it does not touch the contract.

### ④ Design judgment

**should-fix A (new this round) — the repair, now that it writes, is spelled database-wide.** `os migrate stored-expressions --changed --apply` with no `--object` rewrites every stored computed value in the database that differs from its expression, on every object, not the one field the warning is about. The backfill's own text says what that includes: "An expression reading the clock always differs", and the `--changed` flag's description says such an expression "recomputes to the current time". So an author who follows this warning on one drifted field also moves every clock-reading stored value to the time of the run. Those are the values the sibling rule in this same PR calls "sometimes what is meant". The command has the scope flags: `--object NAME`, and `--field NAME` for one field of that object. Name them in the finding and the `os explain` paragraph, for example "run `os migrate stored-expressions --object OBJECT --field FIELD --changed --apply`"; the pass has both names at the call site (`objectName`, `fname`), the member receives only the field's. Round 1 spelled a dry run, so this could not happen then; the prior record asked for `--apply` and did not ask for the scope, so this is a refinement of my own ask, and the command's confirmation prompt and the dry-run sentence stand between the author and the write. Not a blocker; fix here or carry it on the card for the walk.

**nit A — `validate-expressions.ts`, the moved docblock.** The `fieldDefs` docblock is now followed by a line comment and `const servedSelf`, so it documents `servedSelf`, with `fieldDefs` one line below. Putting the line comment and `servedSelf` above the docblock fixes it.

**nit B — `stored-expression-inputs.ts:26`.** The docblock line that gained the `--apply` clause runs to about 140 columns where the block wraps at 80.

**Holds, after trying to break the round's changes.** The position counter against a map-form `objects`, a stack with no extensions (the early return hands back the declared array itself), and a tied extension field (`objectsWithoutTiedFields` maps, keeps positions). The `Clause-②` line against the reader's contradiction and near-miss arms (`yes` with `widening` is neither). "No per-rule switch" against `os validate` as well as `os lint`: `validate.ts` has no flag that excludes a rule from `strictFailing`. The dry-run sentence against `--json`: a dry run there writes nothing either; an apply needs `--yes`. `os build` is named among the commands that print the warnings and is not said to have a `--strict`; it has none.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-t5l85q`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1T5HEokjRgR6vCBX8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ed0f54ed7c91b8fe363e22aaefd8e7608790d6df`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts, content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx + packages/lint/src/stored-expression-inputs.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, .changeset/32529-stored-expression-inputs.md (declaration lines and level only)

Delta round on record 6837689158 (PASS at head `89bb0573` with should-fix A, nit A, nit B). The round's delta is `git diff 89bb0573 ed0f54ed`: two commits (`9dc5296c`, `ed0f54ed`), six files, +34 −19: the changeset, the regenerated `solution-blueprint.mdx`, `rule-explanations.ts`, `stored-expression-inputs.ts`, `validate-expressions.ts` and `solution-blueprint.zod.ts`. `authoring-rules.ts`, `index.ts` and every test file are unchanged since `89bb0573`. Read, not reviewed, on `origin/main`: `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-expressions.ts` and `packages/objectql/src/stored-expression-backfill.ts` (the flags and their scope).

### ① Derived judgments

- **should-fix A (the repair spelled database-wide): discharged as asked; one residual overstatement is should-fix B in ④.**
  - The finding prints the real names. `stored-expression-inputs.ts:237-238` builds `os migrate stored-expressions --object ${objectName ?? 'OBJECT'} --field ${fieldName} --changed --apply` and says why it is scoped (an unscoped `--changed` recomputes every stored value that differs, and one reading the clock always does), keeping the dry-run sentence.
  - `objectName` reaches the member. The new fifth parameter is optional (`stored-expression-inputs.ts:204`); the one call site passes the loop's `objectName` (`validate-expressions.ts:3677`), which is `obj.name` when it is a string and `undefined` otherwise (`validate-expressions.ts:3398`), the same value the finding's `where` already prints (`:3663`). An unnamed object prints the placeholder `OBJECT`, not `undefined`. `fieldName` is the field under judgment, and the member only answers for a non-`formula` field with an `expression`, which is exactly the set `--field` accepts.
  - The flags exist and scope as claimed, on `origin/main`. `stored-expressions.ts:80-89`: `object` is a repeatable `Flags.string`, `field` is "One stored computed field of the one --object" with `dependsOn: ['object']`. `stored-expression-backfill.ts:232-238` refuses a `field` unless exactly one object is named; `:264` sets the scope to `[options.field]` for that object; `:513` rewrites a row only when `hole || (changed && stale)` within that scope. So `--object X --field Y --changed --apply` writes that one field. A name the booted registry does not hold, or a field that is not a stored computed one, is refused before any row is read (`:248`, `:257-262`), so a mismatched printed name fails closed.
  - The other faces spell it scoped: the cross-record `os explain` entry (`rule-explanations.ts:6059-6064`), the member docblocks (`stored-expression-inputs.ts:25-28`, `:196-197`) and the changeset's first bullet. The only unscoped spelling left under `packages/lint`, `content` and this changeset is `rule-explanations.ts:6090`, which is the warning itself.
  - The volatile entry's warning (`rule-explanations.ts:6089-6092`) is true in its first half: the backfill's header says an expression reading the clock "recomputes to the current time, so under `changed` every row of it differs" (`stored-expression-backfill.ts:38-39`), and its report says "An expression reading the clock always differs" (`:596`). Its last clause, "which leaves this one as it was written", holds only when the two fields are on different objects; see should-fix B.
- **nit A: discharged.** `validate-expressions.ts:3581-3585` puts the line comment and `const servedSelf` above the docblock, which now sits directly on `const fieldDefs` (`:3586-3595`). Pure move, no token changed.
- **nit B: discharged.** `stored-expression-inputs.ts:25-30` is re-wrapped; no docblock line of that block passes 80 columns.

### ② Semver level

- **`'@objectstack/spec': patch` is owed and is right.** The round changes one published describe string (`solution-blueprint.zod.ts:255-257`), text only: no key, type, enum, export or parse behaviour moves, and `git diff 89bb0573 ed0f54ed -- packages/spec` is those two lines. The changeset front matter now carries both packages at `patch`, and a bullet names the describe change as "Describe text only". `@objectstack/lint` stays `patch`.
- **Declaration lines unchanged and still true.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with the same three names; `Metadata-protocol: none`. The new optional parameter is on `storedExpressionInputIssues`, which `index.ts:78` does not export (only the two constants are), so it adds no Clause-② name. No narrowing arm, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- **Check-runs on this head: not settled at the time of writing.** 27 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 30 `in_progress` (`Check Changeset`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8, `Test UI` 1/16 to 16/16, both type checks, `Build & E2E UI`); none `failure`. The landing gate reads them when they complete; this record does not claim green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Carried from 6837689158, still the seat's and not in this diff: the HotCRM carrier for `display_title` under `objectstack lint --strict`, and the card for widening the field walk to extension-added expression fields.
- Carried flag closed by this round: the published `STORED_EXPRESSION_RULE` describe no longer names a `summary`. #32703's title ("is refused") is still the seat's to correct.
- The `.mdx` is a generated page; its two changed rows are the describe's new sentence verbatim (two occurrences of the new text, none of the old). No other generated file carries the old sentence: the only other hit for it in the tree is the historical `.changeset/32614-blueprint-expression-stored-use.md:15`, which records what #32614 shipped and is not regenerated.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The describe is accurate against the platform.** The sentence is about a value read from a related record through a reference (`record.customer.name`). A `summary` cannot supply that: it is a roll-up of CHILD records onto the parent with `count` / `sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` (`solution-blueprint.zod.ts:333`, `:653`; `field.zod.ts:2214`), so the old "comes through a `summary`" offered a route that does not exist for a parent's value. The two routes that remain are the two the finding and `os explain` name: a `formula` (shown, not totalled) and a snapshot field written by a flow on the related object when the value changes. The describe, the finding, the explain entry and the changeset now say one thing. A child aggregate is still taught where it belongs, on `summaryOperations`.
- **should-fix B (new this round) — "scoped to the one field" scopes which rows are written, not what each write stores.** The apply is an engine write: `writeUnlessMovedSince` calls `engine.update(object, { id, ...patch })` (`stored-expression-backfill.ts:397-401`), and an engine write computes every stored field of the row. The backfill says so twice: "Because the apply IS a write, it stores every stored field the write computes for that row" (`:41-43`) and "The write computes EVERY stored field of the row, the ones this run was not asked about too" (`:514`). So `--object X --field Y --changed --apply` selects only the rows where `Y` is NULL or differs, and on each of those rows a clock-reading stored field of the SAME object is recomputed to the run time. Three sentences of this round say more than that: `rule-explanations.ts:6091-6092` ("scoped with `--object` and `--field`, which leaves this one as it was written"), the changeset's "The repair is scoped to the one field", and the docblock's "scoped to the one field" (`stored-expression-inputs.ts:26`).
